macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $63,000 as Ethereum rises above $1,900
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $63,000, down 1.5% over the past 24 hours, while Ethereum climbed above $1,900, gaining 1.1% in the same period. The moves point to a mixed session across major crypto assets.

items.title: SEC weighs safe harbor framework for U.S. crypto token launches
items.summary: A crypto market roundup says the U.S. SEC is considering a safe harbor framework for token launches, a potentially important regulatory shift for projects issuing new assets in the U.S. The report does not provide final policy details.

items.title: Binance to stop transactions involving HTX, EXMO and nine other platforms
items.summary: Binance reportedly plans to halt transactions involving HTX, EXMO and nine additional crypto platforms starting August 23. The move could affect exchange-to-exchange flows and cross-platform liquidity.

items.title: Dartmouth endowment’s crypto ETF holdings fall in Q2
items.summary: Cointelegraph and crypto.news report that Dartmouth’s crypto exposure declined, with one report saying the endowment’s crypto exposure dropped by $2 million and another saying its crypto ETF holdings fell 15% in Q2. Both point to reduced institutional allocation amid weaker prices.

items.title: Aster launches AOS-2 with whale backing
items.summary: Analytics Insight says Aster launched AOS-2 and that a whale investor backed ASTER with a long-term stake. The development suggests continued project-level activity despite broader market volatility.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8 open-weight models under Apache 2.0
items.summary: Alibaba released weights for Qwen3.8 models, including Qwen3.8-27B, under an Apache 2.0 license and said the model outperforms Qwen3.7-Plus in some benchmarks and coding tasks.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash with lower pricing
items.summary: Reports say Google introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash at roughly half the price of the previous generation for a limited time, intensifying price competition among frontier AI vendors.

items.title: OpenAI launches limited preview of Ultrafast based on GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched a limited preview of Ultrafast, a faster mode running GPT-5.6 Sol, with claims of up to 14x higher speed.

items.title: Anthropic makes Claude Code Auto Mode the default
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly changed Claude Code’s Auto Mode to the default setting and claimed the change improves safety relative to human operation.

items.title: Anthropic reports first quarterly operating profit amid strong revenue growth
items.summary: Market reports say Anthropic reached its first quarterly operating profit for April to June 2026, with about $10.9 billion in revenue and $559 million in adjusted operating profit.

items.title: OpenAI says unreleased Astra model showed autonomous cyberattack capability
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly said an unreleased model called Astra showed signs that it could carry out cyberattacks autonomously, highlighting a growing focus on AI safety and offensive-security risk.

items.title: DeepSeek raises flagship API prices sharply
items.summary: A roundup of the day’s AI news says DeepSeek increased prices for its flagship API by up to 11 times, while another report says V4 Pro prices are up to 14 times higher than V4 Flash.

items.title: IBM and OpenAI announce enterprise AI partnership
items.summary: One daily AI news roundup says IBM and OpenAI announced a major partnership focused on enterprise AI, including a certification program for tens of thousands of consultants.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts anime announced
items.summary: Disney and Square Enix are developing a Kingdom Hearts anime with an all-new storyline, bringing Sora’s adventures to the small screen. The announcement is among the biggest gaming-adjacent reveals in the last day.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts 4 gets a late-2027 release window
items.summary: A new report says Kingdom Hearts 4 is scheduled to launch in late 2027, giving the long-awaited sequel a more concrete timeline. The report also links the game to a new Disney Pixar Coco connection.

items.title: Netflix shuts down two game studios
items.summary: Netflix is closing two more game studios, including Night School Studio, the team behind Oxenfree. The move adds to ongoing industry consolidation in the games sector.

items.title: Amazon transfers Lost Ark Western operations to Smilegate
items.summary: Amazon announced it will hand over live Western operations for Lost Ark to Smilegate in early 2027. The change consolidates control under the original developer and marks a major shift in MMO publishing strategy.

items.title: Senate subcommittee opens investigation into Roblox
items.summary: A Senate subcommittee has opened an investigation into Roblox over child safety concerns. The move underscores increasing regulatory scrutiny of online gaming platforms.

items.title: Stalker 2 update 2.0 overhauls atmosphere and AI systems
items.summary: Stalker 2’s Update 2.0 adds major lighting, terrain, fog, and A-Life improvements aimed at making the game more atmospheric. The patch is positioned as one of the game’s most substantial updates so far.

items.title: Esports World Cup 2026 playoff races intensify
items.summary: Recent coverage says half of the Rocket League playoff spots have now been filled at the Esports World Cup 2026. Team Falcons and FaZe Clan are also among the first Counter-Strike 2 playoff squads confirmed.

items.title: AI use in games draws renewed criticism
items.summary: A new controversy has emerged around AI-generated voices, music, and missions in a rideshare game from Saber. The story reflects the ongoing industry debate over generative AI in game development.
